title: Horizon-aware mixer scheduler and KV compaction playbook for mixed-length streams
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Summary: We need a repeatable playbook and scheduler prototype that balances latency and GPU memory efficiency for workloads composed of wide-ranging prompt and response lengths (short queries, long-form generations, and multi-turn dialogs). Goal is to reduce p99 latency regressions while increasing effective KV residency and lowering OOM risk on 80GB A100 pools.

Problem statement:
- Mixed-length traffic causes inefficient slot utilization: many short requests prevent coherent coalescing and cause KV fragmentation across GPU slabs.
- Current continuous-batcher heuristics favor immediate dispatch to meet tail-latency SLOs, which increases overall GPU memory pressure and token costs when long responses are scheduled concurrently.
- KV cache residency policy is not tuned for bursty long-response tails; fragments persist and cause slab hot spots and premature evictions.

Objectives:
1) Implement a horizon-aware mixer scheduler that groups slots not only by length but by a short-term horizon estimate (expected remaining tokens) to enable packing short+medium requests together and isolate long-generation slots in presized slabs.
2) Add a KV compaction/passive-merge policy that opportunistically coalesces small KV fragments into contiguous allocations during low-util windows, reducing slab fragmentation and improving residency hit-rate.
3) Define a metrics-backed playbook (experiments, thresholds, rollback criteria) for tuning safe defaults for Dedicated pools and Hosted mixers.

Acceptance criteria:
- p95 latency change <= +5% and p99 latency improvement >= 10% on mixed-length test harness compared to baseline (current continuous-batcher).
- KV residency hit-rate increases by >= 12% for long-session workloads without increasing average token cost by more than 3%.
- No increase in OOM incidents in the test fleet; GPU memory headroom improved on average by >= 6% under identical load profiles.
- Playbook documented with runbook steps, dashboards, and a gated rollout plan (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%).

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Horizon estimator: lightweight exponential moving average of observed remaining tokens per session combined with model-specific generation budget. We avoid heavy ML predictors to limit runtime overhead.
- Packing strategy: prefer pack short requests into mixed slots when estimated combined sequence length stays within slab-friendly boundaries; otherwise isolate long generators to dedicated micro-batches to avoid KV interleaving.
- Latency trade-off: some short requests may incur ~2-5ms added waiting to achieve better packing. Mitigate via latency budget tagging for 'latency-sensitive' routes to bypass packing when needed.
- Compaction cost: compaction will be throttled by a background low-priority worker with rate-limits tied to observed CPU/GPU utilization to avoid interference.

Experiment plan (stepwise):
1) Simulator + replay: run the new scheduler logic in the batch simulator using historical mixed-length traces (prod-sampled week of Feb 2026). Measure expected KV fragmentation, slab utilization, and estimated latencies. Link: https://dashboards.internal/replay/ENG-218432
2) Canary in Dedicated: deploy horizon-aware mixer to 2 Dedicated pools with 10% traffic; enable KV compaction in passive mode (dry-run compaction metrics only). Track p50/p95/p99, KV hit-rate, and eviction counts for 72h.
3) Active compaction: enable actual compaction on a single pool during off-peak window and measure effect on residency and OOMs over 7 days.
4) Gradual rollout using rollout-operator with automatic rollback if p99 increases > 10% or OOMs occur.

Instrumentation & dashboards:
- New metrics: scheduler_pack_ratio, avg_horizon_seconds, kv_fragment_count, kv_compaction_ops, kv_compaction_latency, slab_utilization_by_gpu, scheduler_wait_ms_by_route.
- Dashboards: latency + KV heatmap; follow links in comments and attach to runbook.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: aggressive packing could increase tail latency for latency-sensitive endpoints. Mitigation: explicit route-level bypass and tag-based bypass.
- Risk: compaction induced IO/CPU pressure leading to degraded serving. Mitigation: rate-limited background compaction and OOM circuit breaker that pauses compaction under pressure.
- Risk: estimator mispredictions harming packing quality. Mitigation: continuous feedback loop and fallbacks to conservative packing thresholds.

Next steps (owners):
- Diego: prototype horizon estimator and scheduler changes in the simulator (ETA: 2026-03-03).
- Asha: define compaction heuristics and implement passive dry-run metrics (ETA: 2026-03-05).
- Maya Patel (SRE): create alerting for kv_fragment_count and slab_utilization (ETA: 2026-03-07).
